column2: 中古英语 slypper，由 slip ＋ -er 构成
column3: a light soft shoe worn indoors
column5: She kicked off her slippers by the bed.|One slipper had gone missing.
column6: the shoe the foot slips easily into – 脚一滑就能进去的那种鞋
column7: 拖鞋：室内穿的轻便无带鞋|便鞋：柔软好穿的日常鞋

column2: 中古英语 slipperie，为 slipper（滑的）加 -y 的扩展形 ← 古英语 slipor ← 原始日耳曼语 *slipraz（滑）
column3: hard to stand on or hold because of a smooth wet surface
column5: The wet steps were dangerously slippery.|Fish are slippery to hold.
column6: so smooth that grip is lost – 光到抓不住、站不稳
column7: 滑的：表面不易附着|易滑的：容易让人打滑的

column2: 中古英语 slitten ← 古英语 slītan ← 原始日耳曼语 *slītaną（撕开）← 原始印欧语 *(s)leyd-（撕、裂）
column3: a long narrow cut or opening
column5: Light came through a slit in the curtain.|He slit the envelope open.
column6: a long narrow opening torn or cut – 撕开或切开的一道细长口
column7: 狭缝：细长的开口|切口：刀划出的口子

column2: 早期作 slughorn（战吼）← 苏格兰盖尔语 sluagh-ghairm，由古爱尔兰语 slóg（军旅）＋ gairm（呼喊）构成
column3: a short phrase used to promote an idea or product
column5: The slogan appeared on every poster.|They chanted the same slogan again.
column6: a short cry raised to rally people – 为号召众人而喊出的短句
column7: 标语：写出来的简短号召|宣传语：为推广而用的短句

column2: 由 aslope（斜着）截头而成
column3: a surface with one end higher than the other
column5: The ball rolled down the grassy slope.|The roof slopes towards the back.
column6: a surface tilted from level – 与水平面成角的一片面
column7: 坡：地面倾斜的一段|倾斜：偏离水平的状态

column2: 中古英语 slot ← 古法语 esclot，或出古诺尔斯语 slóð（辙迹）
column3: a narrow opening for putting something in, or a position in a schedule
column5: Put the coin in the slot.|She got an early slot on the programme.
column6: a narrow gap that something fits into – 让东西正好嵌进去的窄口
column7: 狭槽：细长的插入口|位次：安排表上的一个位置

column2: 古英语 slāw（迟钝、缓）← 原始西日耳曼语 *slaiw ← 原始日耳曼语 *slaiwaz
column3: moving or happening at low speed
column5: Traffic was slow all morning.|He is slow to make decisions.
column6: taking a long time to cover ground – 走同样的路要用更久
column7: 慢的：速度低|迟缓的：反应或进展不快

column2: 1812 年起见于记载，原为俚语指「后间」，来源不明
column3: a poor crowded area of a city with bad housing
column5: Families lived in the slum for years.|The city cleared the old slum.
column6: a crowded quarter of poor housing – 住房简陋而拥挤的一片街区
column7: 贫民区：城中贫困住户聚居处|棚户区：以简易房搭成的居住区

column2: 中古英语 sly ← 古诺尔斯语 slǿgr（狡、机巧）← 原始日耳曼语 *slōgiz
column3: clever at deceiving people in a quiet way
column5: He gave a sly glance at the door.|The fox is famously sly.
column6: clever in a way kept out of sight – 机巧而不露在明处
column7: 狡猾的：善用心计不老实|偷偷的：不让人察觉地进行

column2: 古英语 smæl（窄、细）← 原始西日耳曼语 *smal ← 原始日耳曼语 *smalaz
column3: not large in size or amount
column5: They live in a small flat.|Only a small number replied.
column6: taking up little room or measure – 占的地方或量都不多
column7: 细小的：体积或规模不大|少量的：数量不多

column2: 古英语 smeart（刺痛的）← 原始西日耳曼语 *smart ← 原始日耳曼语 *smartaz（疼）← 原始印欧语 *(s)merd-（咬、刺）；「聪明」义由「刺得利」引申
column3: quick to learn and understand, or neat in appearance
column5: She is the smartest student here.|He wore a smart dark suit.
column6: sharp enough to sting – 利到能刺人
column7: 聪明的：理解快、脑子灵|时髦的：装束齐整入时

column2: 来源不明，或为拟声
column3: to break something violently into pieces
column5: He smashed the glass on the floor.|The car smashed into a wall.
column6: breaking something apart with force – 用力使之裂成碎块
column7: 打碎：使物体破成碎片|猛撞：以大力撞上

column2: 中古英语 smellen ← 古英语 *smyllan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *smallijan（燃、冒烟）← 原始印欧语 *smel-（燃、熏）
column3: to notice something through the nose, or a quality noticed that way
column5: I can smell fresh bread.|The room had a strange smell.
column6: taking something in through the nose – 用鼻子把东西接进来
column7: 闻到：用鼻子察觉到|味道：被鼻子察觉的那种性质

column2: 中古英语 smilen ← 中古低地德语 *smîlen ← 古高地德语 smielēn ← 原始日耳曼语 *smilāną ← 原始印欧语 *smey-（笑、喜）
column3: to turn the mouth upward to show pleasure
column5: She smiled at the old photograph.|A faint smile crossed his face.
column6: turning the mouth up to show gladness – 把嘴角向上以示欢喜
column7: 微笑：不出声地笑|笑容：脸上呈现的笑的样子

column2: 由 smoke ＋ fog 混合而成
column3: a mixture of smoke and fog hanging over a city
column5: Smog covered the city for three days.|Heavy smog closed several schools.
column6: smoke and fog settled together – 烟与雾混在一起沉着不散

column2: 古英语 smoca ← 原始日耳曼语 *smukōną ← 原始印欧语 *(s)mewg-（冒烟）
column3: the grey gas given off by something burning
column5: Smoke rose from the small chimney.|He gave up smoking last year.
column6: the grey stream given off by fire – 火所放出的灰色气流
column7: 烟：燃烧产生的灰白气体|抽烟：吸食烟草这件事

column2: 中古英语 smothe ← 古英语 smēþe ← 原始西日耳曼语 *smanþī，更早词源不明
column3: having an even surface with no bumps
column5: The table has a smooth wooden top.|The change went smoothly enough.
column6: even all over with nothing standing up – 通体齐平、没有凸起
column7: 平滑的：表面无凸凹|顺畅的：进行中没有阻碍

column2: 早期作 smuckle，借自荷兰语 smokkelen 或低地德语 smuggeln（潜运）
column3: to move goods illegally into or out of a country
column5: They smuggled the goods across the border.|Someone smuggled a note inside.
column6: moving something across by keeping it hidden – 藏起来运过界去
column7: 走私：非法运货进出关境|偷运：暗中把东西运过去

column2: 借自荷兰语 snacken（咬、吃一点）
column3: a small amount of food eaten between meals
column5: She packed a snack for the journey.|We stopped for a quick snack.
column6: a small bite taken between meals – 正餐之间吃的一小口
column7: 小吃：分量小的简便食物|零食：正餐之外随手吃的东西

column2: 古英语 snaca ← 原始西日耳曼语 *snakō（爬行者），源自 *snakan（爬、滑）
column3: a long thin reptile with no legs
column5: A snake crossed the warm path.|Some snakes hunt at night.
column6: the legless crawler that slides along – 无足而贴地滑行的爬虫

column2: 借自荷兰语或低地德语 snappen（咬、抓）
column3: to break with a sharp sound, or such a sound
column5: The dry branch snapped underfoot.|We heard the snap of a lock.
column6: breaking with one sharp report – 一声脆响之间断开
column7: 啪一声断：一下断开并发出脆响|猛地咬住：突然合口咬上

column2: 中古英语 snacchen ← 古英语 *snæċċan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *snakkjan ← 原始日耳曼语 *snakjaną
column3: to take something quickly and roughly
column5: He snatched the letter from her hand.|A gull snatched the bread away.
column6: taking something away with one quick grab – 一把抓走
column7: 夺过：迅速取走对方手上的东西|抢夺：以强力取得

column2: 或出中古英语 sniken（爬、匍匐）← 古英语 snīcan ← 原始日耳曼语 *snīkaną，拟声起源
column3: to move quietly so as not to be seen
column5: He sneaked past the sleeping guard.|She sneaked a look at the answers.
column6: moving low and quiet to avoid notice – 低身轻步避人察觉
column7: 潜行：不出声地移动|偷偷做：暗中进行不让人知

column2: 中古英语 snesen，为更早 fnesen 的变体 ← 古英语 fnēosan（喷鼻）← 原始日耳曼语 *fneusaną ← 原始印欧语 *pnew-（呼气）
column3: to blow air suddenly out of the nose
column5: Dust made her sneeze three times.|He sneezed into his elbow.
column6: air forced suddenly out through the nose – 气猛地从鼻腔冲出

column2: 中古英语 sniffen，拟声起源
column3: to take air in through the nose to smell something
column5: The dog sniffed at the closed door.|She sniffed the milk carefully.
column6: drawing air in through the nose – 把空气从鼻子吸进去
column7: 嗅：用鼻子辨气味|吸气：把气吸进鼻腔

column2: 古英语 snāw ← 原始西日耳曼语 *snaiw ← 原始日耳曼语 *snaiwaz ← 原始印欧语 *snóygʷʰos
column3: frozen water falling from the sky in white flakes
column5: Snow covered the fields overnight.|It snowed heavily all weekend.
column6: frozen water coming down in white flakes – 结冰的水以白片落下
column7: 雪：从空中降下的白色结晶|下雪：降雪这个过程

column2: 由 snow ＋ storm 复合而成
column3: a storm with heavy falling snow and strong wind
column5: A snowstorm closed the mountain road.|They waited out the snowstorm indoors.
column6: a storm driving heavy snow before it – 卷着大雪的风暴

column2: 古英语 socian（浸、泡）← 原始日耳曼语 *sukōną，为 *sūkaną（吸）的使动形
column3: to leave something in liquid until it is wet through
column5: Soak the beans in cold water overnight.|Rain soaked through his coat.
column6: letting liquid work all the way in – 让液体一直渗进去
column7: 浸泡：放在液体里泡着|吸透：液体渗遍整个物体

column2: 古英语 sāpe ← 原始西日耳曼语 *saipā ← 原始日耳曼语 *saipǭ ← 原始印欧语 *seyb-（滴、渗）
column3: a substance used with water for washing
column5: She washed her hands with soap.|The soap left a faint scent.
column6: the substance that lifts dirt with water – 与水同用能带走污垢的东西

column2: 中古英语 soren ← 古法语 essorer（升空）← 俗拉丁语 *exaurare，由拉丁语 ex（出）＋ aura（气、微风）构成
column3: to rise or fly high in the air, or to increase sharply
column5: An eagle soared above the ridge.|Fuel prices soared that winter.
column6: rising high on the air – 借着气流升到高处
column7: 翱翔：展翅在高空盘旋|猛增：数值急剧上升
